criterion: at least one (glomerulus set, rate) gives a mean Kenyon-cell response fraction inside 5-10% AND activity that does not outlast the odour (post-odour population rate below 1% of the during-odour rate)
reference: In a real fly about 5-10% of Kenyon cells respond to a given odour, each firing a few spikes (Honegger, Campbell & Turner 2011 J Neurosci 31:11772: mean responding fraction <= 0.10; Turner, Bazhenov & Laurent 2008 J Neurophysiol 99:734: 6 +/- 5% of KCs, 2-5 spikes per response).
finding: Sparse, transient Kenyon-cell odour coding is reproduced at 4 glomeruli / 150 Hz: 4.4% of Kenyon cells respond at 0.77 Hz, falling to 0.14 Hz once the odour stops. The rest of the network does not return to baseline (1.69 vs 2.00 Hz per neuron), so the mushroom body recovers while the wider brain does not.
